title: Investigate asymmetric token accounting in partial streaming sessions
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Intermittent discrepancies reported between tokens charged on customer invoices and tokens visible in request/response logs for streaming sessions that terminate early (client-side abort, network reset, or server preemption). Observed behavior shows input tokens sometimes double-counted when a partial response is retried, and output tokens occasionally omitted when a streaming connection is preempted before finalization of usage records.

Observed vs Expected:
- Observed: Some customers see billed token totals higher than the sum of tokens in our persisted request/response artifacts. In other cases, sessions that returned partial output show zero output tokens in final metering records.
- Expected: For every session we should attribute input and output tokens exactly once (idempotent accounting), even across retries, reconnects, and server-side preemption. Partial streams should be charged only for the final accepted tokens or according to the chosen compensation policy.

Reproduction steps (known):
1) Start a streaming chat session using client SDK with streaming enabled and small chunk size.
2) Force a network reset mid-stream (e.g., simulate flaky mobile).
3) Client reconnects with resume token and requests missing suffix.
4) Server may re-emit previously buffered tokens or regenerate those tokens depending on rollback time window.
5) Billing record after session shows both original emitted tokens and resumed tokens credited to same session or sometimes missing emitted tokens.

Hypothesis (root causes to validate):
- Non-idempotent emit path: emitter increments provisional token counters on first send but does not reconcile when a resend/replay occurs.
- Finalization race: session finalizer writes metering rows before KV cache reconciliation completes, causing output token counts to reflect only a subset.
- Reconnect flow writes a separate usage row with overlapping token ranges instead of merging ranges.
- Edge-case: preemption/swap in Dedicated causes in-flight session to be recorded as terminated then resumed on new instance; unique session ID mapping is lost.

Scope: Affects streaming chat/generation endpoints across hosted and Dedicated when sessions experience reconnects, client aborts with retries, or preemption events. Non-streaming (single-response) paths appear unaffected.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Repro steps produce deterministic logs and a test fixture that asserts idempotent accounting for reconnect/resume scenarios.
2) A reconciliation job (or runtime fix) exists that merges overlapping provisional rows into a single final row for each session.
3) Unit + integration tests cover resume, replay, preemption, and client abort patterns.
4) No customer invoices produced in the next billing cycle should show >0.1% discrepancy attributable to this class of bug for affected customers.
5) Instrumentation added to measure provisional vs finalized token deltas per-session in production dashboards.
mitigation_plan:
Short-term: enable emergency guardrail that switches streaming sessions to 'finalize-on-confirm' mode for high-value customers (prevents provisional writes until session close). Also deploy a reconciliation job that dedups overlapping usage rows from the last 48 hours and credits customers if overcharged.
Medium-term: implement session-level idempotency tokens and change emit path to record token ranges without committing billing rows until finalization.
Long-term: update serving runtime to produce deterministic token range metadata (start_offset,end_offset) and store per-chunk checksums so reconstructions are mergeable.
QA_plan:
1) Add synthetic job that simulates 10k reconnect/resume streams with randomized abort timing; assert billing rows equal canonical token consumption.
2) Backfill test using production-like traces from customer X (with consent) replayed into a staging metering pipeline to validate reconciliation.
3) Manual verification: pick three affected customers, run a controlled session with instrumentation, and compare emitted tokens with finalized billing rows.
4) Post-deploy smoke: monitor delta metric (provisional_tokens - finalized_tokens) must be <1% within 24h.
metrics:
Primary dashboards:
- billing.streaming.delta_by_session (time series of provisional vs finalized tokens)
- invoices.discrepancy_rate (percent invoices with reported reconciliation runs)
- streaming.reconnect_rate and streaming.preemption_rate (correlate spikes)
Queries: billing_events SELECT SUM(output_tokens) GROUP BY session_id WHERE finalized=false; metering_reconciliations.count in last 48h.
comments: 2026-02-25 - AP: Filed initial issue after customer report, attached dump and earliest examples. Marking P1 because invoice impact is non-trivial.
2026-02-28 - MR: Added repro harness in staging, confirmed duplicate rows when client reconnects within 3s. Pushed spike PR with extra logging (see links).
2026-03-02 - JL: Observed same pattern in Dedicated; preemption caused session transfer without preserving session_uuid. Raised as dependency for infra (ENG-21802).
2026-03-06 - MR: Implemented reconciliation PoC that merges rows with overlapping token ranges; ran backfill on 48h window, corrected ~0.06% of tokens. Need production hardening.

2026-03-10 - AP: Decided on two-phase plan: (A) short-term guardrails + hourly reconciliation, (B) runtime change to delay provisional writes until finalization. Scheduling follow-up for runtime work in Cycle 2026-W11.
